French = modern spelling (obvious slips and old spellings corrected without marks in the app); each message keeps the printed text in orig.fr (data only, not shown). en · ko translated from the French for this app. Sexual lines and battle reports are left out (see excerpt). Replies and talks are written by this app, not by the recipients.

hint.ko: 남이 어떻게 하기를 바랄 때 que 뒤 동사는 접속법 · je veux que tu sois heureuse, je ne veux pas que tu en aies · être → sois, avoir → aies, venir → viennes
hint.en: When you want someone else to do something, the verb after que is subjunctive · je veux que tu sois heureuse · être → sois, avoir → aies, venir → viennes

hint.ko: 남에게 바라는 일 · I want you to come. I don't want you to worry. · want that you … 는 틀린 꼴
hint.en: What you want another person to do · I want you to come. · not ‘want that you …’

hint.ko: 상대도 아는 일을 일깨울 때 · 약속했잖아요, 좋아하잖아요 · 반말이면 -잖아 · ‘-자나요’는 틀린 꼴
hint.en: Reminds the listener of something they already know · 약속했잖아요 (you promised, remember) · casual: -잖아 · ‘-자나요’ is a misspelling

name.ko: 조건법 과거 (j'aurais voulu · tu aurais dû)
name.en: Past conditional (j'aurais voulu, tu aurais dû)

hint.ko: 지난 일을 아쉬워할 때 · avoir/être 조건법 + 과거분사 · j'aurais voulu, tu aurais dû, ça aurait été · c'eût été 는 옛 글말 꼴
hint.en: Regret about the past · conditional of avoir/être + past participle · j'aurais voulu, tu aurais dû, ça aurait été · c'eût été is the old literary form

name.en: would have / should have + past participle

hint.ko: 지난 일을 되짚을 때 · I would have liked … · You should have come. · have 뒤는 과거분사 (should have came ✗)
hint.en: Looking back at the past · I would have liked … · You should have come. · past participle after have (not ‘should have came’)

hint.ko: 지난 일을 반대로 가정해요 · 같이 있었더라면 좋았을 거예요 · 뒤는 보통 -았/었을 거예요, -았/었을 텐데
hint.en: Imagines the past the other way round · 같이 있었더라면 좋았을 거예요 (it would have been nice if we'd been together) · usually followed by -았/었을 거예요

hint.ko: 뒤 명사의 성 · 수에 맞춰요 · tout le temps, toute la journée, tous les ans, toutes tes lettres · ‘toute triste’ 처럼 형용사 앞에서는 ‘아주’
hint.en: Agrees with the noun after it · tout le temps, toute la journée, tous les ans, toutes tes lettres · before an adjective (toute triste) it means ‘very’

hint.ko: 남의 말을 옮길 때 시제를 하나 뒤로 · “You are sad.” → He told me you were sad. · tell + 사람, say + (to 사람)
hint.en: Passing on what someone said, with the tense moved back · He told me you were sad. · tell + person, say (to + person)

hint.ko: 남의 말을 옮겨요 · 명령은 -(으)라고 (쉬라고 했어요), 서술은 -다고 (슬프다고 했어요) · 줄이면 -(이)래요 · ‘-라구’는 입말
hint.en: Passes on what someone said · orders: -(으)라고 (쉬라고 했어요), statements: -다고 (슬프다고 했어요) · short form -(이)래요

note.ko: 1809년 12월 15일 밤, 튀일리 궁에서 두 사람의 이혼이 선언됐어요. 나라를 이을 아이를 낳아 줄 새 황후가 필요하다는 이유였어요. 이튿날 조제핀은 말메종으로 떠나고, 나폴레옹은 베르사유 정원의 트리아농으로 갔어요. 이 편지는 그 무렵 그녀를 만나고 돌아온 날 저녁에 썼어요. 이 장은 이혼 뒤에도 이어진 편지들이에요. 조제핀은 ‘황후’ 칭호와 말메종을 그대로 가졌고, 둘은 죽을 때까지 편지를 주고받았어요.
note.en: On the evening of 15 December 1809, the divorce of Napoleon and Joséphine was pronounced at the Tuileries: the Emperor wanted a new wife who could give him an heir. The next day Joséphine left for Malmaison, and Napoleon went to Trianon in the park of Versailles. He wrote this letter on an evening in those days, after he had been to see her. This chapter follows the letters that went on after the divorce. Joséphine kept the title of Empress and Malmaison, and the two wrote to each other until her death.

note.ko: 이혼 며칠 뒤, 트리아농의 저녁 일곱 시. 훗날 경찰 장관이 되는 사바리 장군이 말메종 소식을 전해 주었어요. 나폴레옹은 사냥한 고기를 보내고, ‘나도 오늘은 슬프다’ 고 털어놓아요. 이혼 뒤에도 그는 거의 날마다 조제핀에게 짧은 편지를 보냈어요.
note.en: A few days after the divorce, seven in the evening at Trianon. General Savary, later Minister of Police, had brought news from Malmaison. Napoleon sends her game from his hunt and admits: ‘I am sad too today.’ After the divorce he still wrote her short notes almost every day.

note.ko: 1810년 4월, 나폴레옹은 오스트리아 황녀 마리 루이즈와 결혼했어요. 그해 여름 조제핀은 사보이아의 엑스레뱅 온천에 가 있었고, 부르제 호수에서 배를 타다 위험한 일을 겪었어요. 조제핀은 대서양 건너 카리브해의 섬 마르티니크에서 태어났어요. 그래서 ‘바다의 섬 사람이 호수에서’ 라는 농담이 나와요. ‘왕비’ 는 홀란트 왕비 오르탕스, ‘그 남편’ 은 그해 7월 왕위에서 물러난 나폴레옹의 동생 루이예요. 날짜: 받아 본 스캔 한 부는 ‘6월 10일’ 로 읽히지만, 홀(1901)판 등은 8월 10일로 보고 있어요. 호수 이야기도 8월과 맞아요.
note.en: In April 1810 Napoleon married the Austrian archduchess Marie-Louise. That summer Joséphine was taking the waters at Aix-les-Bains in Savoy, and was in danger in a boat on Lake Bourget. She had been born on Martinique, an island in the Caribbean across the Atlantic, hence the joke about an islander of the Ocean dying in a lake. ‘The queen’ is Hortense, Queen of Holland; ‘her husband’ is Napoleon's brother Louis, who had given up the Dutch throne that July. Date: the one scan fetched reads ‘10 June’, but Hall (1901) and others date it 10 August, which fits the lake episode.

note.en: On 20 March 1811 Marie-Louise gave birth at the Tuileries to a son, Napoléon-François, who was given the title King of Rome at birth. Joséphine, at her château of Navarre in Normandy, sent her congratulations; this is Napoleon's reply two days later. The same letter is printed in the Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, vol. XXI, no. 17499. Eugène was Joséphine's son, viceroy of Italy.

messages.fr: J'ai été fâché contre toi pour tes dettes ; je ne veux pas que tu en aies ; au contraire, j'espère que tu mettras un million de côté tous les ans, pour donner à tes petites-filles, lorsqu'elles se marieront.
messages.en: I was angry with you about your debts; I don't want you to have any; on the contrary, I hope you'll put a million aside every year, to give to your granddaughters when they marry.

note.ko: 조제핀은 말메종과 노르망디의 나바르 성을 오가며 지냈어요. 정원 · 옷 · 보석에 돈을 아끼지 않아 빚이 자주 쌓였어요. ‘손녀들’ 은 외젠의 딸들이에요 (오르탕스는 아들만 있었어요). 말메종에는 소를 키우는 작은 농장도 있었어요. 연도: 책에는 ‘181?’ 로 흐리게 찍혀 있고, 홀(1901)판은 빚 이야기 편지 다음인 1811년으로 봐요.
note.en: Joséphine lived between Malmaison and her château of Navarre in Normandy. She spent freely on gardens, clothes and jewels, and often ran up debts. ‘Your granddaughters’ are Eugène's daughters (Hortense had only sons). Malmaison also had a small farm with cows. Year: the printed date reads ‘181?’ in the scans; Hall (1901) places it in 1811, after the letter about her debts.
